newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech dissatisfaction with politics grows - poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech dissatisfaction with politics grows - poll.

text.p: Czech dissatisfaction with the political situation, dominated in recent months by infighting and a low election turnout, has risen to its highest level in recent years, an opinion poll released on Thursday showed.
The poll, taken by the state-funded IVVM agency, showed 58 percent of respondents were rather or very dissatisfied with the state of politics compared with 37 percent who were satisfied.
The poll of 1,001 people was taken between November 1 and 6, shortly before two rounds of voting for the new Senate when turnout was just 35 and 30 percent respectively.
It showed 45 percent of respondents were rather dissatisfied and 13 percent very dissatisfied. A further 34 percent were rather satisfied and only three percent were very satisfied.

The latest overall dissatisfaction rate compared with 56 percent in October and 41 percent in July after inconclusive lower house elections when the centre-right coalition of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus lost its majority.
In recent months both the coalition and opposition Social Democrats have been plagued by internal bickering. Klaus and Social Democrat leader Milos Zeman have also accused each other of being liars.
Analysts say Czechs seem disillusioned with the behaviour of their politicians, a mood reflected in the dismal turnout for the Senate elections earlier this month.
